text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Medical Council of Zambia says it will scrap from its registers doctors selling a drug currently being marketed in Lusaka which claims to cure AIDS.
- A local government workers' strike in the mining Copperbelt Province has spread to Central Province.
- Two journalists on the independent Chronicle newspaper pleaded not guilty to charges of libel and publishing false news with intent to cause alarm.
- Zambia has been invited to attend the eleventh ministerial conference of the Non-Alligned Movement in India in April.
- The opposition Liberal Progressive Front has called on government to collect garbage in the city centre before an epidemic breaks out.
- A Lusaka court is to rule on Wednesday whether the editor of the state-run Times of Zambia should be cited for contempt of court proceedings.
